title: AXI Family Comparison
description: Open each interface family to compare channel structure, burst limits, IDs, ordering, and the design situations each variant fits.

signals.name: AXI3
signals.description: AXI3 defines the five memory-mapped channels, supports 1–16 beat bursts for every burst type, and permits write-data interleaving by carrying WID on the W channel.
signals.direction: Five bidirectionally handshaken unidirectional channels between master and slave interfaces
signals.sampled: Each channel transfers on a rising ACLK edge with VALID and READY HIGH
signals.typicalUse: Legacy high-performance processors and third-party IP
signals.verificationNote: Model WID and legal interleaving only for AXI3; do not apply AXI4 write-data ordering rules blindly.

signals.name: AXI4
signals.description: AXI4 retains the five channels, removes WID and locked transactions, and extends INCR bursts to 256 beats. FIXED and WRAP bursts remain limited to 16 beats.
signals.direction: Five bidirectionally handshaken unidirectional channels between master and slave interfaces
signals.sampled: Each channel transfers on a rising ACLK edge with VALID and READY HIGH
signals.typicalUse: DDR controllers, DMA engines, accelerators, and high-bandwidth fabrics
signals.verificationNote: Check that W data follows write-address order and that a B response waits for both the AW handshake and final W handshake.

signals.name: AXI4-Lite
signals.description: AXI4-Lite keeps the five-channel VALID/READY structure but every transaction is one full-bus-width beat. It normally omits IDs, bursts, and exclusive accesses.
signals.direction: The same AW, W, B, AR, and R channel directions as AXI4
signals.sampled: Each channel transfers on a rising ACLK edge with VALID and READY HIGH
signals.verificationNote: Multiple transactions may still be outstanding. Without IDs, responses must remain in order; do not equate Lite with one-outstanding-only.

signals.name: AXI4-Stream
signals.description: AXI4-Stream is not memory mapped. A source moves an ordered stream of transfer beats to a destination using TVALID and TREADY, with optional packet and byte-qualification sidebands.
signals.direction: One logical source-to-destination stream; TREADY returns from destination
signals.sampled: A stream beat transfers on a rising ACLK edge with TVALID and TREADY HIGH
signals.typicalUse: Video, DSP, networking, and accelerator pipelines
signals.verificationNote: Do not apply memory-mapped burst, response, or address-ordering rules to an AXI4-Stream interface.
